newsitem.title: INDIA: Dollar rise will not hit Japanese economy - Toyoda.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rise will not hit Japanese economy - Toyoda.

text.p: The dollar's rise against the yen on Friday will not adversely affect the Japanese economy, Toyota Motor Corp chairman Shoichiro Toyoda said.
"Not much. But we do not think the fluctuation of the yen against the dollar is very good," Toyoda told Reuters, when asked about the effects of the dollar's rise against the yen.
The dollar hit a four-year peak of 124.34 yen in European trade on Friday, up from its late Thursday level of 123.80/85.

Toyoda, who is here at the head of a Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren) delegation, said: "For us, (from) the perspective of the manufacturers, the reasonable range would be between 100 to 120 yen to a dollar."
He earlier told a business luncheon meeting: "With the yen at 80 (to the dollar), I believe the yen was overvalued. That is more than what reflects the Japanese true strength."

"The exchange rate is determined based on what are called fundamentals, the relative economic strength that the country might have. For manufacturers it is not desirable when the yen-dollar exchange rate fluctuates all of a sudden dramatically," Toyoda told the meeting of the Confederation of Indian Industry.
"So it is desirable that the exchange rate of the Japanese yen vis-a-vis the dollar not move so dramatically within a short period of time," he added.
Toyoda said a rise in the value of the dollar would affect Toyota's performance but refused to elaborate.
"There will be. It depends on how high the dollar moves. Of course depending on how the yen rises or drops it will affect us," he said.
